records.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that combines the strengths of large language models with external knowledge retrieval. Instead of relying solely on the model's internal weights, RAG systems first retrieve relevant documents or passages from a corpus, then use them as context when generating responses. This approach reduces hallucination and keeps answers grounded in the provided sources. Typical RAG pipelines include document ingestion, chunking, embedding, indexing in a vector store, and at query time: embedding the question, finding similar chunks, and passing them to the LLM as context.

Embeddings are dense vector representations of text that capture semantic meaning. Words or sentences that are similar in meaning end up close together in the embedding space. Models like nomic-embed-text produce fixed-size vectors (e.g. 768 dimensions) for any input text. These vectors can be compared using cosine similarity or other metrics to find semantically related content. In RAG, document chunks are embedded and stored; when a user asks a question, the question is embedded and the most similar stored chunks are retrieved and fed to the language model.

Ollama is a tool that runs large language models and embedding models locally. It provides a simple HTTP API, typically on port 11434. You can pull models such as nomic-embed-text for embeddings or llama3 for chat. Running models locally avoids sending data to external APIs and gives full control over the stack. For Kotlin or any language, you can call the /api/embed endpoint with a JSON body containing the model name and the input text to get embeddings for building RAG or search applications.
